mortgage.definition: A loan secured by property, commonly used to buy a home.

auto-loan.definition: A loan provided to an individual for buying an automobile.

personal-loan.definition: Money lent to an individual for personal expenses, typically without collateral, after considering the borrower's reliability and ability to repay.

student-loan.definition: Money borrowed to help pay education costs and repaid under agreed terms.
student-loan.exampleUsage: The brochure explains how a student loan is repaid after study.

line-of-credit.definition: An arrangement allowing someone to borrow money up to an agreed limit.

credit-score.definition: A number based on a person's credit history that lenders may use when assessing borrowing risk.
credit-score.exampleUsage: Paying bills on time can affect a person's credit score.

interest-rate.definition: A percentage showing what borrowing money costs or what saving and lending it can earn over a set period, usually one year.

principal.definition: The original amount of a loan or investment, before interest.

collateral.definition: A security pledged for the repayment of a loan.

co-signer.definition: A person who signs a loan or agreement with the main borrower and accepts responsibility if payments are not made.
co-signer.exampleUsage: The lender explained the responsibilities of a co-signer.

health-insurance.definition: Coverage that helps pay medical and other health-care costs under an insurance contract, usually in return for regular premiums.

car-insurance.definition: Coverage purchased from an insurance company protects people from financial losses linked to owning or using a car.

life-insurance.definition: Insurance that pays an agreed benefit after the insured person dies, according to the policy terms.
life-insurance.exampleUsage: The advisor explained what the life-insurance policy covers.

home-insurance.definition: Insurance that can cover a home, belongings, or certain losses described in the policy.
home-insurance.exampleUsage: They reviewed the home-insurance policy before signing.

travel-insurance.definition: Insurance designed to cover certain unexpected costs or losses connected with a trip.
travel-insurance.exampleUsage: The travel-insurance document lists the situations it covers.

premium.definition: The amount paid regularly for an insurance policy.

deductible.definition: The amount an insured person pays before the policy covers specified costs.

coverage.definition: The total amount and type of insurance carried.

claim.definition: A request for payment from an insurer after a covered loss.

policy.definition: A document setting out the terms and conditions of insurance coverage.

stock.definition: The capital raised by a corporation through the issue of shares entitling holders to an ownership interest (equity).

bond.definition: An investment in which money is lent to an issuer under agreed repayment terms.

mutual-fund.definition: Money from many investors is combined to purchase a broad range of assets.

etf.definition: An investment fund whose shares trade on a stock exchange.

portfolio.definition: A list of the financial assets held by an individual or a bank or other financial institution.

dividend.definition: That part of the earnings of a corporation that is distributed to its shareholders.

capital-gain.definition: The profit created when stocks, property, or a business become more valuable between purchase and sale.

risk.definition: The possibility that an investment will lose money or fail to meet expectations.

return.definition: The money gained or lost on an investment over a period.

diversification.definition: The act of introducing variety (especially in investments or in the variety of goods and services offered).

401k.definition: A U.S. employer-sponsored retirement savings plan funded through employee contributions and sometimes employer contributions.

ira.definition: A retirement plan that allows you to contribute a limited yearly sum toward your retirement.

pension.definition: Money paid regularly to a person after retirement.

social-security.definition: A U.S. program providing retirement, disability, and survivor benefits to eligible people.

annuity.definition: A financial contract that can provide a series of regular payments.

retirement-fund.definition: Money or investments set aside to support someone after retirement.

compound-interest.definition: Interest is added to the original amount, so later interest also grows on those earlier additions.

vesting.definition: The process by which a person gradually gains full ownership of an employment benefit or asset over time.
vesting.exampleUsage: The employee handbook explains the vesting schedule for company benefits.

beneficiary.definition: A person or organization entitled to receive money or benefits.
